description: Our multidisciplinary team works across computational physics, scientific data engineering, AI integration, and interface design. We built T.R.I.A.G.E. end to end: a 1D spherical finite-volume combustion solver in Python and C++, a WebSocket simulation service, NASA PSI ground-truth matching, and a React/D3 dashboard with a two-tier AI analysis layer. We make complex microgravity fire research usable while keeping AI-assisted conclusions traceable to the simulation and experimental data.
summary: T.R.I.A.G.E. is an interactive digital twin for microgravity combustion. It combines a custom 1D spherical finite-volume solver, implemented in Python and C++, with real NASA PSI ACME s-Flame ground truth and a two-tier AI analysis pipeline. A run is visualized as a 2D temperature field and a revolved 3D flame, compared against the nearest real experiment, and ranked by a structured tier-1 verdict. A tier-2 model then synthesizes a fire-safety diagnostic with Moon and Mars ECLSS recommendations. Every AI path has a deterministic local fallback, every chart supports exact cursor readouts, and the dashboard exports a complete A4 PDF report. T.R.I.A.G.E. makes decades of microgravity fire research easier to inspect, compare, and apply to crewed exploration.
details:
T.R.I.A.G.E. (Thermal Reaction Inference & Anomaly Grading Engine) is an interactive digital twin for microgravity combustion. A user configures fuel, oxidizer, oxygen percentage, ambient pressure, gravity mode, mixing strategy, ignition energy, and run length, then executes a 1D spherical finite-volume solver. The solver is implemented twice, as a NumPy reference and a pybind11 C++20 core, so the dashboard uses the compiled path when available and falls back cleanly when it is not. Results appear as a 2D temperature field, an interactive revolved 3D flame, and radial temperature, heat-release, species, and iteration-history diagnostics.

The simulation is compared with real NASA PSI data. A curated ACME s-Flame (PSI-23) ground-truth set, drawn from 286 test points, supplies experimental conditions, burn duration, pressure, and telemetry. A tier-1 matching layer ranks the nearest real test point and returns a structured verdict with the match distance, runner-up, and an explicit no-match state. A tier-2 model then synthesizes a fire-safety diagnostic with Moon and Mars ECLSS recommendations. The UI labels which AI engine answered, and deterministic local fallbacks keep the demo working without external API keys.

The impact is a faster, more transparent path from archival combustion data to fire-safety insight. Missing NASA fields stay null instead of being fabricated, chart tooltips expose exact values, and the dashboard exports an A4 PDF report containing the configuration, outcome, Jev comparison, tier-2 analysis, charts, suggestions, and solver diagnostics. Parameter sweeps, custom fuel presets, and a live calculation log support exploration.

Built with Python 3.12, NumPy, Pydantic, websockets, httpx, pybind11/C++20, React 19, Vite, D3, Three.js, and jsPDF. NanoGPT provides optional Jev and DeepSeek inference, with Azure AI Foundry as a fallback. No GPU or special hardware is required. The key creative choice is using a 1D spherical solver as the single source of truth while presenting it as both a 2D heatmap and a true revolved 3D field, rather than pretending to run 3D CFD.
